themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 17 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 10.24)—suggesting a sudden surge in Uber/Lyft activity, illegal pickups, or traffic obstruction in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 17 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 10.24 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Spike is acute and immediate—likely tied to specific event, service change, or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Interview residents about traffic congestion; map complaint hotspots to identify whether surge is geographically concentrated
Contact TLC and NYPD to determine if there's been a policy shift, app driver recruitment, or loss of enforcement that triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Street Encampments Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 9 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.0 per week over 8 weeks—an 800% increase (z-score: 4.82)—indicating a sudden rise in outdoor homeless camps visible to residents and the city.
evidence: 9 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (800% spike)
Z-score of 4.82 indicates high statistical significance
Community Board budget requests repeatedly ask for 'park safety through more security staff,' suggesting long-standing infrastructure gap that may be enabling encampments
reporting_angles: Canvass specific parks and public spaces (Fort Tryon Park, waterfront areas) to map encampment locations and interview unhoused residents about what prompted the recent influx
Interview Parks Department and NYPD about enforcement capacity and whether recent service cuts or policy changes have made the district less monitored

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—flagging potential unlicensed street food operations, sanitation issues, or territorial conflicts.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Concurrent rise in for-hire vehicles and encampments suggests broader street-use pressure or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Identify the specific locations of the three complaints and interview residents/business owners about sanitation, noise, or congestion caused by vendors
Contact NYC Department of Health and Department of Consumer Affairs to determine whether vendors are licensed and what triggered the spike in complaints

themes_detail.label: Public Urination Spike
themes_detail.summary: Public urination complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—coinciding with the encampment surge and suggesting linked homelessness and sanitation crises.
evidence: 3 public urination complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical deviation
Timing aligns with 800% spike in encampment complaints, suggesting both are symptoms of same underlying homelessness and service delivery crisis
reporting_angles: Interview public health officials about whether recent encampment rise correlates with lack of public restroom access
Report on the relationship between homelessness spikes and sanitation complaints; identify whether city services (restrooms, outreach) are keeping pace with demand

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints rose to 3 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 2,300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—indicating a sudden environmental or disease event affecting street canopy.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Community Board budget requests repeatedly ask for 'park reconstruction or upgrade,' suggesting long-standing maintenance gaps in green infrastructure
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to determine if the three complaints reference the same location or event (pest infestation, disease, weather damage)
Investigate whether recent weather events (drought, storm) or maintenance cuts have accelerated tree decline in the district
